speaker: Brenda Okoro
cascadeSummary: I am holding the line on the two items due this cycle exactly as I promised: the West Oakland charter renewal goes to Council only behind a verified C114 closeout, with the business-and-resident scope and 23-day standard intact, and Grand Lake's $2.5 million gets a Clerk-certified roll call with every Chen-Vega condition written in — no outcome claimed in advance by me. On the ground I go where the mood is souring and the trade is slow: Dimond's culture crisis and the Mayor's town briefing, and Adams Point, where the mood has turned. I back the Mayor where the agenda matches the record I've kept, and I say plainly where a record isn't there yet — Ivy Hill's overlapping filings and Laurel's missing scope stay held, not laundered past a deadline.

statements.topic: West Oakland Stabilization Fund — verified closeout before Council renewal
statements.decision: Hold the C114 closeout verification and Council charter-renewal consideration on this cycle's calendar; no renewal claimed before verification and Council action, with business-and-resident scope and the 23-day standard preserved.
statements.quote: West Oakland gets a verified closeout and a faithful charter renewal — not a shortcut around the businesses and residents this fund serves.
statements.fullStatement: The West Oakland Stabilization Fund is disbursement-active, roughly $20.6 million remaining against the $28 million authorization, and the $400,000 tranche executed under the 23-day standard. The C114 closeout is the record, and the C114 closeout is what goes in front of Council this cycle — verified first, renewal second. Business-and-resident scope stays intact. The 23-day standard stays intact. I will not call a renewal vote before the verification is done and Council acts, because that discipline is the only thing that keeps this fund's integrity when every block wants a piece of it.

statements.topic: Grand Lake Commercial Stabilization — certified full-council roll call
statements.decision: Hold and certify the full-council roll call with all Chen-Vega milestone and audit conditions intact; maintain a YES position without claiming an outcome.
statements.quote: Public money deserves public proof — Grand Lake gets $2.5 million with every milestone and audit condition intact, and every councilmember on the Clerk's record.
statements.fullStatement: Grand Lake has been through committee, through conditions, and through the Mayor's backing. This cycle it gets the recorded full-council roll call, every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition written into the result, and the Clerk certifying the count — not me forecasting it. My position is yes. A position is not an outcome, and I won't pretend it is. The storefronts on that avenue are quieter and the housing pressure is building; they'll know where their councilmembers stood because it will be in the roll call, not in a press line afterward.

statements.topic: Dimond culture crisis and the town briefing — factual record, feet on the ground
statements.decision: Support the Dimond Emergency Town Briefing as the public factual record and next steps for the culture spike, without speculating on causes or linking the separate faith-community responses; commit to being present in Dimond.
statements.quote: Oakland can grieve, organize, and celebrate in the same week — and Dimond gets a factual record and a next date, not a theory about why.
statements.fullStatement: Dimond is the one place in this packet carrying a high-severity culture spike and struggling street trade, and that is where I'll be. The Emergency Town Briefing is the right vehicle: a public factual record and concrete next steps, without me speculating about causes I don't have evidence for and without tying it to the faith-community responses happening elsewhere — Adams Point Methodist's assistance fund, Temple Beth Or's vigil, Masjid An-Nur's grief gathering. Those are their own rooms doing their own work and I honor them separately. Ivy Hill Family Dental closing after eight weeks of decline is its own quiet wound; I'll have names and next dates on it. And Adams Point — mood soured this cycle — gets a visit, not a footnote.

statements.topic: Held filings — Ivy Hill duplication and Laurel scope
statements.decision: Let the Laurel filing deadline pass with INIT-015 held in announced status and let the duplicative Ivy Hill filing (INIT-013) pass rather than submit an overlapping measure; no filing or authorization claimed.
statements.quote: I will not file a third Ivy Hill measure or a Laurel cleanup just to clear a calendar — scope, outreach, and a Clerk record come first.
statements.fullStatement: Two filings I'm holding, and I'll say why plainly. Laurel's $6 million cleanup stays announced: the finished scope and the outreach record aren't there, so letting the deadline pass is more honest than filing something hollow behind it. And the overlapping Ivy Hill measure stays held — INIT-011 is the filed ordinance and it gets its committee hearing on current evidence, but I won't submit a third Ivy Hill measure to look busy. Separate records for separate promises. Where a record isn't real, I'll take the missed deadline over the laundered one.
